Homebound is on a mission to make it possible for anyone, anywhere, to build a home using technology. Created by an experienced team of construction, real estate, design, and technology experts, Homebound is transforming the residential construction industry by improving the costly and inefficient process of building a home.
We’ve created an entirely new way to build homes with technology powering every stage from start to finish to provide a seamless experience for our customers. Homeowners across the country can choose where they want to live, select a home plan that’s perfect for them, then personalize and buy it, all online.

Homebound has raised $150M in capital from leading venture capitalists like Google, Khosla, Thrive Ventures, and we’re scaling quickly in places like Texas, Colorado and Florida. Come build your future with us.

As Senior Product Manager - Field AI, you will own the forward-looking technology that brings AI to the teams building our homes. This is where the physical and digital worlds meet: your users are the Superintendents and Direct Construction Operators (DCOs) on the jobsite, and your product surface spans our mobile application, advanced onsite AI tools, automated data capture, and probabilistic construction schedules with insight analysis.
This is a role for a thought leader in applied AI. We are looking for someone with a strong point of view on how emerging technologies - computer vision, agents, LLMs, and multimodal models - can be applied in a physical, unstructured environment to make our field teams faster, more accurate, and more effective.

You don't need a construction background (though genuine curiosity about the built world is a plus), but you do need real experience translating frontier AI into products that work in the real world, outside the browser.
You'll own the roadmap, execution, and success metrics for the field AI portfolio, and you'll operate as an independent, cross-functional force connecting Construction Operations, Field Operations, and Engineering.

Own the field AI strategy and roadmap: Set the vision and execute end-to-end across the entirety of our field portfolio - from concept to rollout.
Bring AI into the physical environment: Translate the capabilities of computer vision, multimodal models, and agents into products that operate reliably on an active jobsite, where inputs are messy and conditions change daily.
Lead as a thought partner: Bring a strong, well-formed perspective on where field technology is going, and use it to shape how Homebound applies new technologies to the teams building our homes.
Embed with the field: Travel to Texas monthly to work directly with Superintendents and DCOs, run trainings, drive rollouts, and build the tight feedback loops that make field products actually stick.
Drive progress across teams: Operate independently and move initiatives forward across Construction Operations, Operations, and Engineering without waiting for a playbook.
Define product with rigor: Write clear, actionable requirements, establish evaluation and quality frameworks for AI features, and prioritize based on impact, effort, and long-term value.
Measure what matters: Define success metrics and run experiments to systematically improve accuracy, adoption, and field efficiency.

5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of a complex, technical product.
A track record of shipping applied AI products - computer vision, multimodal, LLM/agent-based, or ML systems - that took meaningful action or made decisions in production, not just chat wrappers or lightweight integrations.
Demonstrated experience applying technology in the physical world or in traditionally non-tech, unstructured environments (a strong plus).
Strong technical fluency - comfortable operating alongside engineers and ML teams as peers, reasoning through system tradeoffs, reading evaluations, and diving into the data to answer your own questions.
A self-starter and independent operator who thrives in ambiguity, moves quickly, and drives outcomes cross-functionally without heavy process.
A genuine thought leader in emerging AI - you follow the frontier closely and have a point of view on how to apply it.
0→1 product building: hands-on experience taking a product from concept through launch to real-world adoption.
Exceptional communication skills and the ability to translate seamlessly between field needs, technical teams, and executive leadership.
Willingness to travel to Texas monthly to work shoulder-to-shoulder with our field teams.
Interest in construction and the built environment is a plus; no prior industry experience required, but an expectation to learn the domain rapidly.

Airtm is a financial-infrastructure company building the future of the online-work economy. We are on a mission to empower the world's growing number of Digital Entrepreneurs in the Global South, giving them the financial freedom to thrive.
The problem is clear: in emerging markets, accessing the dollar economy is difficult. Cross-border payments are slow, expensive, and often lose value to inflation. This limits the potential of millions of talented individuals.
Airtm’s solution is a swift and comprehensive financial platform that facilitates low-value cross-border payments and local cash-outs. As pioneers in stablecoin-payment infrastructure, Airtm has built the most advanced cross-border payment system available on the market.
As a company married to the world of online work, Airtm will go beyond payments to build the necessary infrastructure the online-work economy needs to thrive. Own the product Vision: Define, communicate, and drive the product strategy and roadmap for your product scope, ensuring alignment with programme direction and wider business objectives

Champion Modern Product Practices: Embed Agile, Lean, and continuous discovery methodologies into the team’s DNA, fostering a culture of high performance, accountability, and customer empathy.

Nium provides global infrastructure for real-time cross-border payments. We were founded on the mission to deliver the global payments infrastructure of tomorrow, today. Our platform enables banks, fintechs, and global businesses to move money instantly, everywhere.
Co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore with offices in 14 markets worldwide, we are entering one of the most exciting chapters in our journey. In March 2026, we delivered the largest month in our 11-year history with record revenue, record volumes, and EBITDA profitability. Today, Nium moves nearly $60B in payments annually, almost entirely for enterprises, while continuing to strengthen an already healthy balance sheet.
It is an incredible time to join us, and we are only just getting started.
Our payout network spans 190+ countries and 100 currencies, with 100 + corridors in real time. We power seamless transfers to accounts, wallets, and cards, support local collections in 35 markets, and as a principal card issuer on Visa, Mastercard, Discover, and UATP, Nium issues over 50 million card tokens every year.

Backed by regulatory licenses in 40+ markets, we make it simple for our partners to onboard, integrate, and scale globally.

This scale and innovation have earned us recognition as one of CNBC’s World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025, winner of Best Cross-Border Payments Solution at the PayTech Awards, and inclusion in FXC Intelligence’s Top 100 Cross-Border Payments Companies list.
In 2024, we raised US$50 million in Series E funding at a US$1.4 billion valuation to accelerate network expansion, product innovation, and talent growth. With the B2B payments market projected to hit US$175 trillion by 2030, Nium offers ambitious builders the chance to shape the future of global money movement with the scale of a leader and the energy of a high-growth company.

Nium has built the licensing, regulatory, and infrastructure position across the EU and UK. Direct SEPAconnectivity, a growing client base, and a licensed presence across European markets — the foundation is in place.What comes next is the product and commercial layer: activating the right products in the right markets, in theright sequence, and building a commercial motion that converts that position into sustained revenue.

We are hiring a Staff PM to lead that effort, based in London. The scope is broader than a single market or productline. This PM owns the European market — commercial outcomes, product activation, and client relationshipsacross the EU and UK — and will take on meaningful product and segment ownership beyond the regionalmandate, including areas where Nium has live products that need dedicated product leadership to grow.

Own the European market
Define which of Nium's products to activate in which markets and in what sequence. Own the volume targets and clientactivation milestones. Be Nium's product authority in enterprise conversations — the person the commercial team relieson when a deal turns on a product question, and the PM who is in the room when it matters.
Translate regulation into product decisions.
PSD2, PSD3, the EU instant payments mandate, and FCA requirements are the framework within which you makeproduct decisions — what needs to be built, in what order, and when it is ready to go live. Regulatory fluency is aproduct skill this PM brings and applies directly.
Drive commercial activation
Build and own the commercial proposition for Nium in Europe: right-to-win positioning, ICP definition, and a product-ledapproach to growing the pipeline. Travel payouts is a named early segment; the model you develop extends from there.You work closely with the European commercial team and are in the room with enterprise buyers when the discussionturns substantive.
Expand product ownership over time
Nium has live products adjacent to this role — including account validation and pull payments — that will benefit fromdedicated product leadership as this PM establishes their position. You will identify what to take on and when,collaborating with product and engineering teams across the globe and driving outcomes without direct team authority.

You have substantive experience building in European payments. You have owned a product through PSD2compliance, launched on SEPA or UK Faster Payments rails, and made product decisions within a regulatoryframework. The output is something shipped and live.
You think commercially. You know which segments to prioritise, how to develop a right-to-win argument that holds upin a competitive market, and how to contribute meaningfully in an enterprise conversation when the discussion turnstechnical. You have been in those rooms.
You work well without a complete playbook. You set direction and work through product and engineering teamsglobally without direct line authority. You take initiative and bring others with you.
You use AI seriously and at scale — to compress execution and carry more scope than a traditional IC model allows.The time it frees stays on judgment: commercial decisions, regulatory calls, client relationships.
You are looking for a role where the scope grows with you. If you have built strong products and are ready for thenext challenge to be owning a market — and then expanding well beyond it — this is worth a conversation.
8+ years in product management. European payments, fintech, or financial infrastructure required. SEPA or UKFaster Payments depth is a strong signal. Experience at a PSP, neobank, or payments infrastructure company atscale is the most relevant background.

Internal product ownership

Adoption and business impact

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles.

We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

About Supabase
Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.
More than 10 million developers build on it, from solo founders shipping over a weekend to teams and builders via Vercel, Lovable and Stripe, and every one of them reaches Supabase through a surface: an API, an auth flow, an SDK, or a Partner's product with Supabase integrated.
The current and next wave of software leans on those surfaces harder than any before it.
Agents now act on behalf of developers and end users, authentication has to work machine-to-machine as seamlessly as it once worked human-to-human, and independent platforms increasingly need to authenticate, delegate, and coordinate with each other without a person in the loop.

For a platform built on Postgres with Auth, Compute, Storage and generated Data APIs at its core, the surfaces where Supabase meets Partners and their systems are some of the most important avenues that we own - this role owns these surfaces.
This role owns a focused portfolio of those Partners. Not the platform as a whole, but a small number of strategic Partners whose integrations you are accountable for making excellent. Success here is a product measure, not a commercial one: the integration is high quality, the developers who use it are well served, and it keeps improving.

That means living close to those developers, obsessing over where the integration fails them, and turning what you learn into the roadmap. It is a product and engineering job first, because the best integrations are won in architecture reviews and pull requests, not in meetings.
What You'll Be Responsible For
Owning the success of a focused portfolio of strategic Partners, a small number of them rather than the platform as a whole. You are accountable for the outcome of each partnership: a high-quality integration that the developers who use it reach for, and that keeps getting better.
Living close to the developers who use these integrations. Talking to them constantly, finding where each integration breaks down in real use, and building the roadmap from that signal rather than from a Partner's wishlist.
Deciding the right integration model for each Partner: what Supabase owns, what the Partner owns, what you build jointly, and what stays open and Partner-agnostic, reading whether the two roadmaps run together or diverge and choosing accordingly.
Working hands-on with each Partner's product and engineering counterparts to ship. Holding your own in an architecture review and a code-level design discussion, and turning strategy into shipped, high-quality integrations rather than long conversations.
Setting the quality bar for what a great integration looks like, and building the mechanisms (documentation, tooling, guardrails, versioning) that hold every Partner to it as adoption scales.
Defining what success looks like for each integration and measure it honestly: adoption by the developers who use it, integration quality, and reliability in real use. Using those signals to decide how deep to go with each Partner and where to push the integration next.

s.h: You Might Be a Good Fit If You
s.t:
Have 7+ years of product management on developer tools, or are an ex-founder with strong product instincts, and are technical enough to read an architecture doc, follow a design discussion, and ask the right questions.
Are based in the San Francisco Bay Area. While we hire globally for almost all roles, this role requires being located near SF.
Have shipped integration or platform surfaces that other companies' systems build against, owning APIs, auth or identity flows, or developer-facing platform surfaces end to end, and can reason at the product level about how two independent systems should authenticate and exchange data: where to be open, where to be strict, and where trust lies in these integrations.

Familiarity with more recent primitives like workers/agent sandboxes and developer-tooling products, or with machine-to-machine authentication, is a bonus.
Are biased toward speed, and would rather ship something imperfect (but secure) while learning than spend another month polishing a spec.
Build with what you own, using the surfaces on your roadmap the way a Partner would: standing up an auth flow, calling the Data API, deploying a database, wiring Supabase into another product. You form opinions through first-hand use.
Comfortable using AI tools to compress the slower parts of the role, like research, drafting, and synthesising feedback, so you spend more time on judgment calls.
Work async by default. Supabase is fully remote, so you make decisions in writing and move work forward without meetings.

Fully Remote
We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.
Tech Allowance
Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.
Annual Off-Sites
Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.
Flexible Work
We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.
Professional Development
Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

Who is Heidi?
Heidi is building an AI Care Partner that supports clinicians every step of the way, from documentation to delivery of care.
We exist to double healthcare’s capacity while keeping care deeply human. In 18 months, Heidi has returned more than 18 million hours to clinicians and supported over 73 million patient visits. Today, more than two million patient visits each week are powered by Heidi across 116 countries and over 110 languages.
Founded by clinicians, Heidi brings together clinicians, engineers, designers, scientists, creatives, and mathematicians, working with a shared purpose: to strengthen the human connection at the heart of healthcare.
Backed by nearly $100 million in total funding, Heidi is expanding across the USA, UK, Canada, and Europe, partnering with major health systems including the NHS, Beth Israel Lahey Health, MaineGeneral, and Monash Health, among others.
We move quickly where it matters and stay grounded in what’s proven, shaping healthcare’s next era. Ready for the challenge?

Heidi's core products are expanding in both scope and reach. Scribe already powers more than 3 million patient consultations a week, and Evidence and Remote are scaling behind it. We're now building out the New Bets function to create the next wave of new products.
This is a zero-to-one product role inside a company that already has proven impact and partnerships with the NHS, which is the combination every early-stage PM wants and almost never gets. Most v1s launch into silence.

Yours go in front of clinicians who already open Heidi every day, and who will tell you within a week whether you've built something they need. You can ship on a Tuesday, watch a GP use it on a Thursday, and know where you stand by Friday.

In addition to the external feedback loop, within the London Office, we have Clinicians sat within Customer Success, Regulatory Compliance and GTM, so there is plenty of lived experience within reach.
You'll own new bets end to end, not features on someone else's roadmap. You take a problem space from conviction to evidence: frame it, size the prize, prototype it, put it in front of real clinicians, and make the call. A few bets become Heidi's next product line. Most don't. Killing them cleanly, quickly and without ceremony is as much the craft as scaling the winners.
A small dedicated squad sits alongside you to build and test. If it needs a pilot scoped with a health system, you scope it. If it needs a landing page, you write it.
You might already be a PM. You might be a strategy consultant who is tired of recommending and wants to own what happens next. You might have run operations and spent the last two years fixing the product from the outside. The title matters less than the pattern: you build things, you move fast, and ambiguity makes you sharper, not slower.

Own each bet end to end: the problem it goes after, why it matters now, and the goals and success metrics you set and are held accountable to
Take each bet from thesis to evidence - frame the problem, size the prize and define what "working" means before anything gets built
Prototype fast, often yourself: a v0 built in Cursor or Claude Code beats a sprint of engineering time spent on the wrong thing
Get out of the building: sit in clinics, watch how visits actually run and turn what you see into the next sprint
Design pilots with commercial and regional teams that produce a decision. Think real accounts, real usage, honest numbers
Make the scale-or-kill call and own the narrative with founders, leadership and customers
Do whatever the bet needs: pricing, positioning, onboarding, the launch email. There's no one else to hand it to, which is the point
Graduate the winners into staffed product lines with roadmaps someone else can run, then start again

They often arrive faster than any one team can act on them. Someone has to bring order to that stream, tell apart what a customer wants from what a customer needs, and turn it into a coherent product direction across different product areas.
In this high-impact role, you will own the relationship between Elastic Security's product organization and our most strategic enterprise accounts. You will manage enhancement requests across many enterprise customers at once.

You will prioritize them with judgment and data, and make sure they keep transitioning through the system instead of sitting idle.

You will be the person a CISO trusts in the room, the person an engineering lead respects for the quality of your requirements, and the person who can tell a major customer that something will not be built without losing the relationship.

You will work at the intersection of Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Engineering, building the structure that lets Elastic scale close customer relationships without simply adding headcount.
What You Will Be Doing
Own the enhancement request pipeline across multiple strategic enterprise accounts at once. Build and maintain a structured system to track, prioritize, and respond to customer-sourced requirements, and keep requests moving rather than leaving them in “under consideration.”
Translate customer requirements into shipped products. Work at the level of customer pain, not just the feature that was asked for, and synthesize input from many accounts into a single, coherent product direction.
Turn input from strategic accounts into successful products. Look for patterns across accounts. Shape some of these patterns into formal partnerships for design. Make sure the resulting capabilities benefit the wider market, not just the single customer that made the request.
Feed validated customer patterns back into the core product roadmaps, influencing direction well beyond the accounts you cover.
Serve as the primary product voice in meetings with senior customer stakeholders, including the CISO, CTO, and VP of Security Operations. Deliver roadmap updates, including deprioritizations and misses, in a way that keeps the relationship deep.
Prioritize customer-sourced requirements using structured frameworks such as RICE, weighted scoring, and opportunity sizing. Use data where it is available and clear judgment where it is thin, and be transparent about which is which.
Partner with product and engineering leads to write requirements they can act on without follow-up clarification meetings. Understand system architecture well enough to assess feasibility and scope on your own.
Operate across Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Legal. Support deal cycles as a product resource through RFP responses, security questionnaires, and roadmap presentations to prospects.
Navigate tension between a customer's contractual expectations and the internal roadmap , and tackle it directly rather than through routine escalation.
Create artifacts such as roadmap trackers, enhancement request dashboards, and decision memos that give customers and internal stakeholders visibility without requiring a meeting.
Advocate for customer needs inside the company while resisting the pull of the loudest or largest customer setting the roadmap at the expense of the broader market.

Extensive Experience: 7–10 years of product management experience, with at least 4 years in B2B enterprise software. A consistent record of owning a product area with meaningful revenue impact and of leading products from customer input through shipped, iterated outcomes. Direct experience working with named strategic accounts, not only through customer success proxies. Experience with hyperscalers, MSSPs and/or PubSec is a solid plus.
Security Domain Knowledge: Hands-on knowledge with SIEM, SOAR, XDR or broader security operations platforms, either as a product manager or as a practitioner such as a SOC analyst, detection engineer, or security architect.

You can credibly discuss detection engineering, log ingestion pipelines, correlation rules, threat hunting workflows, and compliance use cases without a solutions engineer in the room. You understand the difference between what a CISO wants to hear and what a SOC analyst actually needs.

A background as a security practitioner, such as SOC, incident response, or detection engineering, before moving into product is a solid plus, and brings credibility that is hard to teach.
Enhancement Request Management at Scale: You have personally run a structured enhancement request pipeline across several enterprise accounts at the same time. You can step into a relationship with dozens of open requests and no prior documentation and build a working tracking system within weeks.
Executive Presence: You are comfortable as the primary product voice with C-suite and VP-level customer stakeholders. You can deliver difficult news without losing the relationship, and you can hold both the executive view and the analyst view in the same meeting.
Technical Credibility: You earn respect from engineering through the quality of your requirements rather than through authority. You write specs engineers can act on, and you know enough about architecture to judge feasibility and scope.
Cross-functional Leadership and Influence: You have operated at the intersection of Product, Sales, Customer Success, Engineering, and Legal, and you know which function owns what and how to advance work across all of them. You lead across a matrixed organization, align multiple stakeholders toward a common vision, and drive execution in a dynamic, remote-first environment, with the autonomy and judgment expected of a principal-level product leader.
Structured Thinking and Bias for Closure: You bring order to unstructured problems, using data to prioritize and clear judgment when data is thin, and staying transparent about which is which. You move work through the system and follow up proactively rather than waiting to be asked, defaulting to visibility through artifacts instead of meetings. You advocate for customer needs while synthesizing them into product direction rather than relaying demands.

We’re hiring a Staff Product Manager to own the core marketplace experience. We’re rethinking things from the ground up—you won’t be inheriting a roadmap, a backlog, or a set of conventions. You’ll be building the product from the ground up alongside the CPTO.
This role requires someone who thinks in systems. A marketplace is not a single product—it’s an ecosystem. You’ll need to hold the consumer experience, the practitioner experience, the matching logic, the trust and safety layer, the business model, and the growth loops in your head simultaneously, and make smart tradeoffs between them every day.
You will report directly to the CPTO and work alongside a small, senior engineering team. There are no layers between you and the work, and no layers between you and the decisions that shape the company.

Product Strategy & Vision
Define the product vision and strategy for the marketplace, grounded in deep user understanding, competitive analysis, and a clear-eyed view of the business model.
Own the roadmap end-to-end. Decide what to build, what to kill, and what to sequence—with conviction, not consensus.
Develop and maintain a strong point of view on where the wellness and longevity market is heading and how our product should evolve to lead, not follow.
TRUE 0→1 product thinking: identify the fastest and cheapest ways to validate core assumptions before committing significant engineering investment.
Marketplace Systems Thinking
Design and optimize both sides of the marketplace: the consumer journey (discovery → trust → booking → retention) and the practitioner journey (onboarding → activation → growth → advocacy).
Develop frameworks for marketplace health: supply/demand balance, liquidity metrics, matching quality, and network effects.
Own the cold-start playbook. Figure out how to bootstrap supply and demand in new verticals and geographies.
Think critically about marketplace trust and safety—credential verification, reviews, dispute resolution—as a product surface, not an afterthought.
Execution & Shipping
Partner with engineering and design to ship continuously. Write clear, opinionated specs. Run structured discovery. Make scope decisions that keep velocity high.
Instrument everything. Define success metrics for every feature. Run experiments. Kill things that aren’t working.
Balance competing priorities across consumer, practitioner, and platform workstreams while maintaining a clear view of the overall system.
Business & Growth
Own the business logic of the marketplace: pricing models, take rates, subscription tiers, transaction economics.
Partner with growth and marketing on acquisition loops, activation funnels, and retention strategies for both sides of the marketplace.
Use data to identify the highest-leverage opportunities. Build the instrumentation and dashboards needed to operate with clarity.
AI as a Force Multiplier
AI should be part of your daily operating system as a product manager.
Research synthesis: distilling user interviews, market data, and competitive intel at speed.
Spec and strategy drafting: using AI to accelerate writing, then applying your judgment to sharpen it.
Data analysis: querying, visualizing, and interpreting data with AI assistance.
Prototyping: rapidly generating UI concepts, user flows, and copy variations.
Workflow automation: building personal and team workflows that eliminate toil.
Bring a perspective on how AI should be woven into the product itself—personalized recommendations, intelligent matching, automated practitioner tools.
Raise the AI fluency bar for the entire team. Share what’s working. Push others to adopt.

Experience & Background
7+ years of product management experience, with significant time on marketplace, platform, or multi-sided products.
You’ve been a startup founder, a founding PM, or an early employee who built 0→1 products with limited resources. You know what it’s like to ship when there’s no playbook, no established process, and no safety net.
You’ve operated at the Senior, Staff, or Principal level—or you’ve functioned at that altitude regardless of your title (common for founders and early-stage operators).
Proven ability to ship products that drive measurable business outcomes, not just features.
Domain Passion
You are passionate about wellness, longevity, and preventive health. This isn’t a box you’re checking—you have a personal connection to this space. Maybe you’ve seen the healthcare system fail someone you love. Maybe you’ve gone deep on your own health optimization. Maybe you’ve worked in healthtech and know firsthand how much better it could be.
You stay current on trends in functional medicine, longevity research, consumer health, and the evolving practitioner landscape.
Working Style
Exceptional product taste. You see what’s working, what’s not, and what’s missing—and you care about the details.
Clear, precise communicator—in writing, in specs, in conversation, and in a room with engineers.
Comfortable with ambiguity and pace. You don’t need permission to act. You don’t wait for perfect information.
Strong analytical chops. You pull your own data, run your own analyses, and let evidence shape your decisions.
Low ego, high ownership. You do what needs to be done—whether that’s writing a spec, responding to a user complaint, or fixing a broken onboarding email.

Direct experience in health, wellness, longevity, or consumer health—and an understanding of the regulatory, trust, and compliance dynamics of the space.
Experience building or scaling a marketplace through cold-start, supply/demand balancing, and network effects.
Experience building AI-native products (not just AI features bolted onto existing workflows).
Technical depth—you can read code, write SQL, or prototype in no-code/low-code tools.

At Too Good To Go, we dream of a planet with no food waste.
Did you know that more than 40% of all food produced gets thrown away? This unnecessary food waste — and the resources needed to produce and transport it — accounts for 10% of global greenhouse gas emissions.
Too Good To Go is a certified B Corporation on a mission to end food waste. We connect stores with surplus food to consumers across 20 markets in Europe, North America, and APAC — with over 140 million registered users, more than 200,000 daily active stores, and 600 million meals saved from going to waste.
Why This Role
Pricing sits at the centre of everything we do. It shapes what partners earn, what consumers pay, and how much surplus food actually gets saved. Today, pricing decisions are made in different places, for different reasons, without a single team owning the strategy end to end.
We are changing that. We are building our first dedicated Pricing team — and you will be the founding member.
You will start with a concrete, high-value problem: the pricing infrastructure behind our Key Account deals. That's your launchpad — from there, you will have real scope to shape our approach to dynamic pricing, consumer-facing service fees, and pricing strategy across Too Good To Go more broadly. This is a role built for someone who wants to define a domain, not just execute a brief.
The goal behind everything we do is twofold: save as much surplus food as possible, and grow the pie between TGTG, our Partners, and our Consumers — never trading one off against the other.
There is a further dimension to this. We are expanding beyond food into new non-food, non-perishable categories — and that growth brings pricing complexity and opportunity we have not had to solve before. Getting ahead of that, rather than reacting to it, is part of this role.

As Senior Product Manager for Pricing, you will build the foundation for how Too Good To Go prices its marketplace — starting with Key Account deals, then extending across the business.
In the near term, you will design and ship the infrastructure that lets us set, manage, and evolve pricing for Key Account partnerships with the flexibility our commercial teams need.

From there, you will develop a smarter, more dynamic pricing algorithm that responds to supply, demand, and partner economics — replacing static rules with something genuinely intelligent. Alongside this, you will investigate our consumer-facing service fees: how they're structured, how they're perceived, and where there is room to optimise.
Underneath all of it are two questions you will own: how do we price in a way that saves as much surplus food as possible, and how do we grow the pie for everyone — Too Good To Go, our Partners, and our Consumers — rather than shifting value from one side to another? Answering both well means understanding marketplace pricing broadly: the best practices and patterns other two- and three-sided marketplaces use, and what applies to ours.
Pricing decisions rarely stay inside one product's boundaries, so you will work across product teams and the wider organisation — Commercial, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, and Key Accounts — to make sure pricing is right everywhere it shows up, not just within your own roadmap. You will become the go-to person for anything pricing-related at Too Good To Go, including presenting your strategy and results to the Global Management Team.
You will also help lay the pricing groundwork for our move into non-food, non-perishable categories — different cost structures, margins, and purchase patterns than the food pricing we know today, and a chance to shape pricing thinking for a new part of the business from the start.

You will be the founding Pricing PM, operating as an individual contributor, with a small dedicated engineering team of around 3-4 developers to start. We will grow the team's scope and headcount as we prove impact, not before. You will report directly to our VP of Product.
This is a new team with a clear starting point, not a fixed script. You will know where to begin — Key Account deals — but how the team's remit, roadmap, and impact grow from there is largely yours to shape. If you want a role where everything is already solved and you are just executing, this isn't it. If you want to help define what great pricing looks like across Too Good To Go, it is.
The role is suited to someone who does not need daily direction — who can set the agenda within that mandate, manage up effectively, and make strong pricing calls with incomplete information.

Build the pricing infrastructure for Key Account deals, giving commercial teams the tools and flexibility to structure partnerships well while keeping pricing logic sound and scalable.
Design and develop a smart pricing algorithm — moving from static, rules-based pricing toward a dynamic model informed by supply, demand, and partner-specific economics.
Investigate consumer-facing service fees: how they're set, how they perform, and how they should evolve to balance consumer value with business sustainability.
Take a holistic view of pricing across TGTG, Partners, and Consumers — optimising for meals saved and for growing the pie for all three, rather than trading one off against another.
Research and apply best practices and patterns from marketplace pricing more broadly, adapting proven approaches to our specific dynamics rather than reinventing from scratch.
Own the roadmap and OKRs for the Pricing team within its agreed mandate, sequencing the work so that early wins on Key Accounts build toward the algorithm and fee strategy.
Work across product teams and the wider organisation — Commercial, Data Science, Engineering, Finance, and Key Accounts — to make sure pricing decisions are right wherever they show up, not just within your own roadmap.
Be the go-to person for anything pricing-related at Too Good To Go, including presenting strategy, models, and results to the Global Management Team.
Anticipate the pricing complexity and opportunity of TGTG's expansion into non-food, non-perishable categories, and start laying the groundwork for pricing them well.
Use data rigorously — pricing experiments, elasticity analysis, partner and consumer feedback — to test hypotheses before scaling them.

Multi-year experience in Product Management with direct, hands-on ownership of pricing.
Experience with pricing in a marketplace or platform business is a genuine differentiator. If you've worked on take rates, dynamic pricing, two-sided pricing trade-offs, or fee structures in a marketplace, you will hit the ground running.
A track record of building pricing algorithms, models, or infrastructure — not just adjusting numbers in a spreadsheet, but shipping systems that price things well and can evolve over time.
Comfort working with quantitative teams (data science, analytics, finance) to translate pricing theory into production systems.
How you work
You are comfortable — and genuinely thrive — working independently, with a high degree of autonomy, especially in the early stages of building a new team.

As a Product Manager at Grafana Labs, you'll develop a vision and strategy for your product domain. You will own your product’s roadmap, collateral, and market research, and you will collaborate with Grafana leadership on fine-tuning your product’s goals.

You will be the primary advocate and expert in your area, with a strong ability to communicate needs, functionality, and details effectively both to external customers and internal stakeholders. The teams and people you will be interacting with will be 100% remote and globally distributed, so strong and proactive communication is essential.
Product Managers are the bridge that connect Engineering, Design, and UX to GTM. You are a facilitator who ensures the free flow of information across these teams and are expected to be technically proficient when representing our products to our customers.

As the Staff Product Manager for OpenTelemetry Experience, you’ll own the end-to-end journey for helping people and agents instrument workloads and successfully send useful OpenTelemetry data to Grafana Cloud.
Your mission is to make Grafana Cloud the easiest and most trusted destination for OpenTelemetry workloads. You’ll reduce the uncertainty, complexity, and failure points users encounter between deciding to adopt OpenTelemetry and receiving healthy, correctly attributed, and actionable telemetry in Grafana Cloud.
Teams can instrument workloads, directly or with the help of coding agents, through OpenTelemetry SDKs, automatic instrumentation technologies such as Beyla and SDK injection, or client-side OpenTelemetry Collectors. Each path presents different decisions, deployment requirements, configuration steps, and potential failure modes.

You’ll define a coherent experience that helps users choose the right approach, complete setup successfully, troubleshoot problems, and understand whether their telemetry is healthy and useful. You’ll design a future in which a growing share of instrumentation work is performed by coding agents acting on behalf of developers.

This means treating agents are first-class participants in the experience and ensuring that instrumentation options, configuration requirements, errors, and validation signals are structured, discoverable, and actionable by both humans and machines.

OpenTelemetry SDK onboarding and configuration
Automatic instrumentation experiences, including OBI/Beyla and SDK injection
Client-side OpenTelemetry Collector deployment and onboarding
Collector configuration, authentication, and initial connectivity
Guidance and machine-readable context that help people and agents choose the right instrumentation approach
Workflows that allow coding-agents to implement, configure and verify instrumentation safely
Troubleshooting missing, incomplete, malformed, or unhealthy telemetry
Validation signals that allow both people and agents to confirm that telemetry is healthy, correctly attributed, and usable in Grafana Cloud
The transition from receiving telemetry to activating the appropriate Grafana Cloud observability solution
Success does not stop when Grafana Cloud receives the first data point. Telemetry must arrive with the quality, context, and structure required to support meaningful observability outcomes. You’ll partner closely with teams responsible for experiences such as Application Observability, Kubernetes Monitoring, Infrastructure Observability, and Drilldown Apps to ensure OpenTelemetry workloads receive a first-class experience from initial setup through first value.
This is a horizontal Staff-level product leadership role spanning multiple products and engineering teams. You may not directly own every SDK, collector, instrumentation technology, or downstream application involved in the journey. You will, however, be accountable for the coherence of the overall customer experience, its success measures, and the cross-product strategy required to improve it.
AI will also be part of how you work, not only what you build. You’ll be expected to use AI tools regularly to accelerate customer-research synthesis, analyze product signals, explore technical workflows, prototype experiences, develop positioning content, and test agent-led instrumentation journeys. You’ll model thoughtful, hands-on adoption of AI while applying strong judgement to its outputs.
The role is not focused on developing OpenTelemetry as an open source project in isolation. You’ll engage with and contribute to the OpenTelemetry ecosystem where appropriate, while measuring success through customer activation and outcomes in Grafana Cloud.

Define the vision, strategy, and cross-product roadmap for the journey from an uninstrumented workload to healthy, useful telemetry in Grafana Cloud solutions
Create coherent, opinionated experiences that help users choose and implement the right approach across SDK instrumentation, automatic instrumentation, and Collector-based deployment while preserving the flexibility advanced users require
Identify and eliminate the leading causes of setup failure, abandonment, misconfiguration, and low-quality telemetry
Establish shared experience principles, priorities, and success criteria across the product and engineering teams contributing to the OpenTelemetry journey
Use customer research, product data, and market insight to prioritize investments and measure outcomes such as onboarding completion, time to useful telemetry, telemetry health, and workload expansion
Partner with downstream Grafana Cloud solution teams to create a coherent transition from telemetry ingestion to meaningful product activation

MongoDB is seeking a strategic and execution-oriented Senior Product Manager to own the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of Revenue and Order to Cash (OTC) capabilities that enable accurate, scalable, and efficient revenue operations.
This role will work closely with the Group Product Manager, Quote to Cash (QTC), owning the OTC and revenue processes within the broader QTC organization, while partnering across Finance, Revenue Operations, Sales, Enterprise Architecture, Engineering, and Program Management to improve the end-to-end order-to-cash lifecycle — order management through billing, collections, revenue recognition, and close — and help the business scale with reliable, increasingly automated revenue systems.
You will own product discovery, prioritization, requirements, delivery partnership, and launch readiness across the OTC and revenue lifecycle — including order management, subscription and contract operations, billing, accounts receivable, collections, renewals, revenue recognition, month-end and quarter-end close, and ERP integrations.

The central focus of this role is revenue accuracy and timeliness: reducing manual adjustments, strengthening SOX and audit controls, accelerating time to invoice and cash, and building a foundation for continuous process improvement across the revenue lifecycle.

Define and maintain the Revenue/OTC product vision, strategy, roadmap, and release priorities in alignment with company objectives, with revenue accuracy and close efficiency as the north star
Partner closely with the Group Product Manager, QTC to align the OTC and revenue roadmap with the broader Quote to Cash strategy, while owning the order-to-cash and revenue processes as your dedicated area of focus
Build deep expertise in NetSuite and the surrounding revenue systems landscape, including billing, accounts receivable, revenue recognition, month-end and quarter-end close, order management, contract and subscription data, ERP integrations, and related Finance and GTM systems
Elicit, analyze, and document business and functional requirements across the OTC lifecycle; translate them into clear epics, user stories, acceptance criteria, and an actionable product backlog
Lead prioritization across competing Finance, Revenue Operations, and Sales needs, balancing near-term business value with long-term scalability and architectural health of revenue systems
Partner with Stakeholders, Lead PdM, Engineering, Architecture, TPM/Program Management, and implementation partners to evaluate and integrate strategic first- and third-party solutions for OTC and revenue processes
Define success metrics and KPIs for Revenue/OTC initiatives — such as billing accuracy, days sales outstanding (DSO), manual journal entry volume, and close cycle time — using data and stakeholder feedback to validate assumptions and measure post-launch outcomes
Own and improve end-to-end revenue workflows across order capture, billing, accounts receivable, collections, renewals, revenue recognition, month-end/quarter-end close, and reporting, including support for subscription and consumption-based business models
Provide product oversight for revenue controls, data definitions, business logic, integrations, and the overall consistency of the user experience across OTC systems
Coordinate integrated, cross-functional testing and partner with technology and business leads on release strategy, change management, training, and adoption for revenue system changes
Identify opportunities to improve revenue accuracy, accelerate time to invoice and cash, reduce billing leakage and manual journal entries, strengthen auditability and SOX compliance, simplify close processes, and maximize the return on investment of Revenue/OTC products
Communicate product decisions, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, and progress clearly to stakeholders and executive audiences, with particular fluency in revenue and close-related metrics

Required Experience and Skills
8+ years of relevant product management experience, with a proven track record of delivering enterprise business systems and influencing stakeholders at all levels
Strong experience with Order to Cash (OTC), Quote to Cash, or adjacent revenue and finance processes, with a clear emphasis on the order-to-cash and revenue recognition side of the lifecycle
Hands-on understanding of NetSuite-based billing and revenue operations, revenue recognition, accounts receivable, collections, month-end and quarter-end close, order management, subscription and contract data, and ERP or downstream revenue integrations
Strong NetSuite product and integration experience, with a solid understanding of Finance operations, revenue accounting, billing controls, SOX/audit requirements, and the upstream GTM processes that drive downstream revenue outcomes
Experience working with Agile/Scrum delivery teams as a Product Owner or equivalent product leader
Strong data analysis and metrics skills, including the ability to define revenue and close-related KPIs (e.g., DSO, billing accuracy, close cycle time) and use quantitative and qualitative inputs to drive prioritization
Experience managing complex integrations, data models, business rules, and dependencies across enterprise revenue platforms
Demonstrated success collaborating across Finance, Revenue Operations, Sales, Engineering, Architecture, and other cross-functional teams
Experience with consumption-based, subscription, or other complex commercial business models is a plus
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience; advanced degree is a plus
Personal Attributes
Strategic thinker who can connect revenue systems decisions to business and financial outcomes
Detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable managing multiple priorities and dependencies across the OTC lifecycle
Strong communicator who can make complex technical, financial, and operational topics clear to varied audiences
Effective decision-maker and problem solver who brings structure to ambiguity, especially around revenue controls and close processes
Self-motivated, adaptable, collaborative, and able to influence without direct authority
Customer- and stakeholder-focused, with a strong bias toward measurable revenue outcomes and continuous improvement
Why This Role Matters
Order to Cash is a critical business capability connecting commercial execution to accurate billing, cash collection, revenue recognition, and financial reporting. In this role, you will help make the revenue lifecycle a scalable business enabler by improving revenue integrity, strengthening NetSuite and related system foundations, accelerating cash realization, tightening SOX and audit controls, and reducing operational effort and risk across the OTC and close process.

Payments is at the heart of Monzo. It’s how our customers move, receive, spend and manage their money, from cards and bank transfers to cross-border payments, merchant acquiring, payment experiences in the app, and the platform infrastructure that underpins the whole bank.
This role sits in our Payments Platform area, working most closely with our Finance Infrastructure squad. The squad sits in Payments, but partners deeply with Finance teams to build the systems, abstractions and capabilities Monzo needs to operate safely, scale efficiently, and expand into new markets.

You’ll work on foundational financial infrastructure: the ledgers, data, controls, reporting, reconciliation and platform capabilities that help Monzo understand, account for and manage money across the bank.
This is a role for someone who gets genuinely excited by complex, technical infrastructure. The work is often behind the scenes, but it’s business-critical: it helps Monzo scale, launch new products and markets, support Finance, and keep the bank running safely.

Defining the product strategy and roadmap for Finance Infrastructure within Payments Platform.
Partnering closely with Engineering, Finance and Payments leaders to understand what Monzo needs from its financial systems today and as we scale.
Moving the team from reactive delivery towards a more strategic, product-led approach, asking why we’re building things, what good looks like, and how today’s choices support Monzo’s long-term needs.
Translating complex finance, accounting, operational and regulatory needs into scalable platform capabilities.
Prioritising across competing stakeholder needs, balancing urgent delivery with long-term system health.
Helping Monzo build financial infrastructure that can support multiple products, entities, countries, currencies and regulatory environments.
Building trusted relationships with senior stakeholders across Finance, Engineering, Product and Operations.
Bringing strong product discipline, technical curiosity and systems thinking to a space that is critical to Monzo’s future growth.

You’re excited by “boring but critical” infrastructure, things like ledgers, reconciliation, financial data, controls, reporting, internal platforms, abstractions or backend systems.
You can work with senior and cross-functional stakeholders, including Finance, Engineering, Product and operational teams.
You’re comfortable bringing product thinking into ambiguous or stakeholder-heavy environments, and moving teams from request-led delivery towards long-term strategy.
You’re high-agency, ambitious and excited to stretch yourself in a team with a high bar.
You care about customers and business outcomes, even when the work is several layers removed from the end customer experience.

**Unser Development-Bereich betreut das Herzstück von Finnova - unsere Kernbankensoftware. In der Abteilung «Core & Regulations» suchen wir für das agile Scrum-Team «Gebühren, Tarife und Geldwäscherei» eine engagierte Persönlichkeit als Product Owner.

In dieser Schlüsselrolle übernimmst du Verantwortung für ein zentrales Produkt und gestaltest dessen Weiterentwicklung gemeinsam mit unserem Product Management sowie einem interdisziplinären Scrum-Team aktiv mit.

Dabei bringst du neue Ideen ein, setzt Impulse für kundenorientierte Lösungen und trägst dazu bei, unsere Kernbankensoftware fit für die Zukunft zu machen.**
## Du begeisterst dich für... ##
* die aktive Weiterentwicklung und die kontinuierliche Optimierung unseres Core-Banking-Produkts, um gemeinsam mit dem Produktteam die Produktstrategie erfolgreich umzusetzen und das Produkt auf das nächste Level zu heben
* die fachliche Führung eines crossfunktionalen Scrum-Teams nach agilen Prinzipien und die Förderung einer Kultur der Eigenverantwortung
* die Erfüllung der hohen Ansprüche unserer Finnova-Banken hinsichtlich Qualität, Stabilität, Sicherheit und Skalierbarkeit
* die enge Zusammenarbeit mit internen und externen Stakeholdern, um fachliche Anforderungen zu verstehen und in hochwertige Lösungen zu überführen
* die Pflege, Priorisierung des Product Backlogs, um den Kundennutzen und die Wertschöpfung der Produktentwicklung zu maximieren
* die Sicherstellung qualitativ hochwertiger und termingerechter Auslieferungen im Einklang mit der Product Roadmap
## Du begeisterst uns... ##
* mit einer abgeschlossenen höheren Ausbildung in Wirtschaftsinformatik, Banking & Finance oder einer vergleichbaren Qualifikation mit mehrjähriger Berufserfahrung und fundiertem bankfachlichem Know-how
* mit deinem ausgeprägten Fachwissen im Core Banking, insbesondere in den Bereichen Gebühren, Tarife und Geldwäscherei
* mit deiner nachweisbaren Erfahrung als Product Owner oder Senior Business Analyst in agilen Softwareentwicklungsprojekten
* mit deiner starken Kommunikationsfähigkeit im Umgang mit unterschiedlichsten Stakeholdern, von Kunden und Fachbereichen bis hin zu Softwareentwicklern
* mit deinem Gespür für Priorisierung sowie deinem konsequenten Fokus auf maximalen Kundennutzen
* mit deiner analytischen und konzeptionellen Arbeitsweise sowie mit deiner innovativen und teamorientierten Persönlichkeit
* mit verhandlungssicheren Deutsch- und Englischkenntnissen

Every CodePath learner engages our platform, whether they are a college CS student in a direct course, a student at a partner university, an alum sharpening their skills, or a working engineer retraining for the AI era. The Senior Product Manager, Learner Platform Experience owns this platform.
CodePath's courses work because they are intensive, industry-vetted, and human. The hard problem is scale. As we grow from tens of thousands of learners toward millions, the quality and effectiveness of the learner experience on the platform has to improve, not dilute.

That demands an AI-First approach: clearly and thoughtfully identifying where AI can accelerate effectiveness, productivity, and scale, and where human connection and touchpoints are essential to maintain motivation, commitment, and progress. Getting that boundary right is the core judgment call of this job, and you will make it over and over.
The ownership lines are clear. Curriculum owns what we teach. The Learning team owns how it is taught, including the live classroom. You own the platform: everything a learner touches when they log in, from the course portal to asynchronous engagement between sessions to the touchpoints that keep them moving. You will collaborate closely with Learning so the platform powers great live delivery, but the platform experience is yours.
Success looks like measurable acceleration in the rate of learning, retention, and engagement, even as the number of students grows by an order of magnitude.
Two things make this role unlike most PM jobs
Learning rate is the scoreboard. Plenty of platforms can deliver content at scale. Almost none can prove their students learn faster because of them. You will be measured on outcomes, retention, and engagement, not feature velocity.
The ceiling is enormous. Every course CodePath delivers, direct or through partners, rides on the platform experience you build. As we scale to an order of magnitude of more students, your decisions compound across every learner we will ever serve.

Form Health is a virtual obesity medicine clinic delivering physician-led, evidence-based care for obesity and related cardiometabolic conditions. Obesity affects more than 40% of U.S. adults, and as GLP-1 medications reshape the field, Obesity and Cardiometabolic Medicine is in a period of rapid growth and opportunity. Form Health is at the forefront of that shift, building a clinical model that combines rigorous, personalized medical care with the technology to make it accessible at scale.
Every Form Health patient works closely with a dedicated multidisciplinary Care Team, including board-certified physicians (many ABOM-certified, and endocrinologists), advanced practice providers, and Registered Dietitians who together deliver comprehensive, one-on-one treatment that includes nutrition, behavioral health, physical activity, and FDA-approved medication, if appropriate.

Through our mobile app, patients engage in regular video visits along with text messaging, photo journaling, and personalized educational content. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of clinical care and to treating every individual with empathy and respect.
Founded in 2019, Form Health is a venture-backed, mission-driven company partnering with leading employers and health plans to expand access to high-quality, guideline-based obesity and cardiometabolic care nationwide. We're deeply invested in our core value of putting patients first, and equally committed to building a culture where every employee is valued and we learn and grow together.

The Care Delivery team builds the tools that let our clinical team run a high-performing virtual practice — from prescribing and prior authorizations to the day-to-day workflows clinicians rely on to do their best work with patients.

This role is highly visible within Form Health : the tools you ship directly shape how our clinical team practices and, downstream, how our patients experience care.

We're looking for someone who's genuinely energized by hard, regulated, multi-stakeholder problems — with clinical, patient, payer, and operational constraints — as well as someone who uses AI as a real part of supercharging their work, rather than a buzzword on a resume.
This role will report to our Lead Product Manager for Care Delivery, with significant ownership from day one and plenty of room to help shape how the practice scales as the team grows. This role is fully remote and can be located anywhere in the U.S. ( Note: while not required, it is beneficial to be in or close to the Eastern Time zone given frequent collaboration with our Boston-based clinical and operations leaders)

Identify where AI and automation can responsibly reduce clinical or administrative burden (e.g., documentation, prior-auth workflows, care coordination), and partner with engineering to evaluate and ship those capabilities thoughtfully

We Breathe Life Into Data
At Komodo Health, our mission is to reduce the global burden of disease. And we believe that smarter use of data is essential to this mission.

That’s why we built the Healthcare Map — the industry’s largest, most complete, precise view of the U.S. healthcare system — by combining de-identified, real-world patient data with innovative algorithms and decades of clinical experience.

The Healthcare Map serves as our foundation for a powerful suite of software applications, helping us answer healthcare’s most complex questions for our partners.

Across the healthcare ecosystem, we’re helping our clients unlock critical insights to track detailed patient behaviors and treatment patterns, identify gaps in care, address unmet patient needs, and reduce the global burden of disease.
As we pursue these goals, it remains essential to us that we stay grounded in our values: be awesome, seek growth, deliver “wow,” and enjoy the ride. At Komodo, you will be joining a team of ambitious, supportive Dragons with diverse backgrounds but a shared passion to deliver on our mission to reduce the burden of disease — and enjoy the journey along the way.
The Opportunity at Komodo Health
Komodo Health's AI Platform and Services organization builds the platform every AI product at Komodo runs on: agent infrastructure, evals, data context, and the surfaces customers touch. Small pods build on shared primitives and ship in weeks. Product managers here build the first versions of what they propose and to iterate alongside their teams quickly.
The suite that built this business was designed for an analyst at a screen. The platform underneath it now reasons. Our flagship product Navigator runs investigations that used to take a person weeks, and an ai-augmented product suite interoperates with it to streamline workflows. We are just getting started. What the next generation of the suite actually is remains an open question, and today it needs ownership.
That question is this seat. You will define the next generation of Komodo's product suite and prove it by building it. The current surfaces are your material and your distribution. The mandate is what comes after them. Principal here means your answer sets the pattern for every surface that follows.
Looking back on your first 12 months at Komodo Health, you will have…
Put a thesis on record for what the next generation of the suite is, argued in working software customers have touched, and won cross-functional and leadership support for it.
Built the first version of at least two new products from that thesis yourself, then ran a pod of four or fewer from prototype to GA with no dedicated project management.

Own the thesis for what customers touch. Study how they actually work, decide what should exist, and revise the argument as models improve.
Build first versions with AI tools and platform primitives. Bring engineering in to scale what shows value, and drop what does not.
Deploy forward. Work inside customer environments where necessary, scope in real time during contracting cycles, and treat deployment as part of the product.
Propose and defend the shape of the growing portfolio. As the new generation lands, you decide what the existing solutions become.
Set the pattern. Your architecture and your build habits become how the surface pods around you work.

At Komodo, we're not just witnessing the AI revolution – we're leading it. This is a pivotal moment in time, where being first to market with AI transforms industries and sets the bar. We Breathe Life Into Data
At Komodo Health, our mission is to reduce the global burden of disease. And we believe that smarter use of data is essential to this mission.

That’s why we built the Healthcare Map — the industry’s largest, most complete, precise view of the U.S. healthcare system — by combining de-identified, real-world patient data with innovative algorithms and decades of clinical experience.

The Healthcare Map serves as our foundation for a powerful suite of software applications, helping us answer healthcare’s most complex questions for our partners.

Across the healthcare ecosystem, we’re helping our clients unlock critical insights to track detailed patient behaviors and treatment patterns, identify gaps in care, address unmet patient needs, and reduce the global burden of disease.
As we pursue these goals, it remains essential to us that we stay grounded in our values: be awesome, seek growth, deliver “wow,” and enjoy the ride. At Komodo, you will be joining a team of ambitious, supportive Dragons with diverse backgrounds but a shared passion to deliver on our mission to reduce the burden of disease — and enjoy the journey along the way.
At Komodo, we partner with organizations throughout the healthcare ecosystem to improve patient care and reduce disease burden through data-driven insights.

As a member of the Data Product team, you’ll help us to build a best-in-class healthcare data architecture covering hundreds of millions of patients through tens of billions of transactions that provides the foundation of that mission. Our people are the center of our success.

We are a smart, supportive team with diverse perspectives and a shared passion for fixing what’s broken in healthcare. It’s fun, challenging and important - and we’re looking for folks with a shared mindset to join our team.
We’re looking for a Senior Data Product manager to help drive the development and innovation of our core data products. In this role, you’ll work with engineers to drive our product strategy and execution on Komodo’s growing suite of data products.

You’ll work with engineering leadership to help craft our technical strategy based on your deep understanding of our platform and customer needs. As a Data PM, you’ll work closely with our product principal and commercial teams to document use cases, create requirements, design evaluation criteria, and ensure on-time high-value analysis.

You’ll own the day to day responsibilities for sprint management, and will ensure that the team is operating at high levels of efficiency. You’ll also work cross-functionally to ensure collaboration with teams throughout the organization, and will help to share knowledge throughout the company.
Developed real fluency in our data through a customer lens
Led discovery into a set of customer use cases and built an evidence-based point of view on where Komodo is uniquely positioned to win
Shipped marked improvements to one or more core data products
Identified, scoped, and validated at least one new data product opportunity or significant enhancement to an existing product
Built a prioritized, evidence-backed backlog that the team and stakeholders trust
Earned trust as a thought partner to Data Engineering and the commercial-facing team
Experience in a data-focused role at a B2B technology or software company, with prior product management experience a strong plus
Real technical depth, including the ability to write and understand SQL, reason about data models and pipelines, and engage substantively with engineers on tradeoffs rather than relaying messages between them and the business
Working knowledge of the core concepts behind statistical data analysis, and the judgment to notice when they are being misapplied
Experience with US healthcare data, and an understanding of the questions life sciences teams bring to it
Curiosity about how data and systems are built and where they break, paired with the drive to go find the answer and comfort in not knowing something for a while
A bias toward the simple version, with the patience to sit with an ambiguous problem and ask the question that reframes it rather than shipping the first workable answer
The ability to break a conceptual goal into smaller, actionable pieces, with enough attention to detail to define what "done" and "good" mean before work starts
A drive to understand our customers deeply, and to translate that understanding into requirements precise enough to build from
Fluency with AI tools as part of how the work actually gets done, including exploring unfamiliar datasets, prototyping concepts, drafting and pressure-testing requirements, and challenging their own reasoning

At Hudl, we build great teams. We hire the best of the best to ensure you’re working with people you can constantly learn from. You’re trusted to get your work done your way while testing the limits of what’s possible and what’s next. We work hard to provide a culture where everyone feels supported, and our employees feel it—their votes helped us become one of Newsweek's Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces .
We think of ourselves as the team behind the team, supporting the lifelong impact sports can have: the lessons in teamwork and dedication; the influence of inspiring coaches; and the opportunities to reach new heights. That’s why we help teams from all over the world see their game differently. Our products make it easier for coaches and athletes at any level to capture video, analyze data, share highlights and more.
Ready to join us?

We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our Athlete Performance group. You’ll be responsible for a product suite that supports sports scientists and coaches in capturing and analysing athlete monitoring data—whether from wearables, optical tracking, or other data sources—to mitigate injury risk, optimise athletic performance, and track the physical development of athletes.

s.h: As a Senior Product Manager , you’ll
s.t:
Grow our human performance business . You’ll work with a cross-functional team to create a coherent product strategy and vision, connecting it to the wider company strategy and effectively delivering against it. You’ll “quarterback” a key investment, with the goal of building products that customers love and use daily.
Advocate for the product. You’ll develop a deep understanding of our customers and our business needs, building trusting relationships with customers and senior internal stakeholders. You’ll also help practitioners tell a fully contextualised story by combining athlete monitoring data with Hudl’s unique video and match analysis assets.
Motivate your squad . This is critical—you’ll determine what success looks like and work across multiple functions to turn your product vision to reality.
Foster collaboration. While balancing cost, timeline and customer benefit, you’ll also work with Marketing, Sales and Customer Support to develop go-to-market plans.
Time spent collaborating with your teammates in-office will be a regular part of how you work. We’re currently considering applicants within commuting distance of London. You’ll be expected to work more days in-office than remote, but will have the freedom to coordinate your specific in-office schedule with your team.
Must-Haves
Experience . You’ve spent more than four years in product management roles within agile software development environments. You can work largely autonomously, and you have a proven track record of delivering valuable customer-facing software.
Dependable. You can be counted on to find the right information to make a decision, and you own them after they’re made.
Grit. You don’t let setbacks get you down—instead, you come through and deliver for customers.
A self-starter. You can balance your time between working with your squad, running discovery and defining strategy. You also know how to get the job done and can roll up your sleeves and get hands on when necessary.

Follow a lean way of working and a continuous improvement mindset within the product management team.

TOLEDO is a global leader in precision instruments and services.
